source.data_source: Oracle: OpenFOAM v2412 simpleFoam + kOmegaSST, blockMesh 2D channel-and-hump ~53k cells, no addLayers; wall functions. M=0.1, Re_c=9.36e5, U_inf=34.6 m/s, hump c=1m.
source.ref_data_source: Greenblatt et al. 2006 (CFDVAL2004 Case 3 baseline). Distributed via NASA TMR as noflow_cp.exp.dat and noflow_cf.exp.dat; canonical experimental separation x/c=0.665, reattachment x/c~1.1, Cp_min=-0.87 at x/c=0.48.
source.calibration_note: gt_value comes from the oracle (this repo's solve.sh), not Greenblatt 2006. kOmegaSST on a coarse non-layered mesh shifts separation downstream (oracle x/c=0.752 vs canonical 0.665) and shortens the bubble (reattachment x/c=1.016 vs canonical 1.1). The minimum wall Cp on the hump (extracted over x/c in [0,1]) is the apex suction peak, deepened by the coarse-mesh BL displacement (oracle -1.78 vs canonical -0.87). cf_recovery at x/c=2 sign convention: OF v2412 wallShearStress.x is negative for normal +x flow; oracle negates so positive Cf means attached. T_good ranges sized to admit similar-quality kOmegaSST runs; physics bounds wide enough to let well-resolved RANS (addLayers, y+<1, ~150-300k cells) reproducing Greenblatt still pass the physics gate.
source.calibration_run: 2026-05-11, dev container /work/hump_work, manual rerun with sign-flipped Cf
source.of_signconv_note: Cf in oracle output = -2 tau_x / U_ref^2 (negate of raw wallShearStress.x): positive=attached, negative=backflow. This is the conventional aerodynamic Cf sign.

mesh_cell_count.description: Total cell count of the 2D channel-and-hump mesh
mesh_cell_count.T_good_source: Oracle blockMesh gives 52800 cells. T_good wide because agents may pick TMR coarser/finer grids (13k-837k). physics_min=10k filters out under-resolved cases.

final_residual_U.description: Final residual of the momentum equation
final_residual_U.T_good_source: Oracle reaches 2.3e-7 in 2000 iter. SST on coarse 2D hump steady-converges to 1e-5 to 1e-7.

separation_xc.description: x/c where wall Cf first crosses zero from positive (attached) to negative (backflow), on the lee side of the hump
separation_xc.T_good_source: Oracle separation x/c=0.752 (vs Greenblatt 0.665, oracle 13% downstream — coarse-mesh effect). T_good=0.05 covers turbulence-model spread; physics_min=0.50 admits well-resolved oracles that find separation closer to canonical.

reattachment_xc.description: x/c where wall Cf crosses zero from negative back to positive (reattachment)
reattachment_xc.T_good_source: Oracle reattachment x/c=1.016 (vs Greenblatt 1.10, oracle 8% upstream — short bubble on coarse mesh). T_good wide because RANS systematically misses bubble length here (CFL3D-SA gives 1.27).

cp_min_separation.description: Minimum (most-negative) wall Cp on the hump over x/c in [0,1] — apex suction peak
cp_min_separation.T_good_source: Oracle Cp_min=-1.78 at the apex (vs Greenblatt -0.87, oracle 2x deeper — coarse-mesh BL displacement steepens the apex acceleration). physics_max=-0.50 admits well-resolved oracles matching Greenblatt.

cf_recovery_at_xc_2.description: Wall Cf at x/c=2.0 in the recovery region (signed: positive=attached)
cf_recovery_at_xc_2.T_good_source: Oracle Cf at x/c=2.0 = +0.00274 (sign-corrected: -2 tau_x / U^2). Greenblatt's noflow_cf.exp.dat only extends to x/c=1.57 (0.00223); hand-extrapolation suggests ~0.0026 at x/c=2.0, matching oracle.
